post.description:
Real session invalidation: the current token's `jti` is added to a
Redis revocation set for whatever time remains until its natural
expiry, so it is rejected by decode_token() on every subsequent
request — not just discarded client-side. This is the local-session
half of logout for both password and SSO logins; see
POST /auth/sso/logout for the additional IdP-side (RP-initiated)
logout step.

get.description:
Tenant-scoped: an admin only ever sees users in their own tenant,
platform-admin status notwithstanding — user management stays a
per-tenant operation.

post.description:
Platform-admin only. A brand-new tenant otherwise has no member who
could ever log into it — /auth/users always scopes the new account to
the CREATING admin's own tenant (by design, so a tenant admin can never
provision a user into a different tenant). So this optionally
provisions the new tenant's first admin atomically with the tenant
itself, which is the only place a user is ever created outside the
creator's own tenant, and only because the platform admin is not
creating it for themselves.

get.description:
Public (no auth) — the login page must be able to call this before
the user has signed in, to decide between a real 'Continue with SSO'
button and an honest 'SSO unavailable' message. Never returns a secret.

post.description:
Revokes the local session exactly like POST /auth/logout, and — only
when the configured provider actually advertises RP-initiated logout
(an `end_session_endpoint` in its discovery document) — also returns
that URL for the frontend to navigate to. If the provider doesn't
support it, this says so honestly rather than claiming IdP logout
happened.

get.description:
Non-secret SSO configuration for the Administration page. Never
includes OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET or any token — only whether it's set.

Detailed dependency/service state — status is derived from the
actual checks below, never hardcoded 'ok' regardless of what they find.

Process-alive check only — deliberately makes no dependency calls.
If this process can respond at all, it is alive; whether it can
actually SERVE traffic (dependencies reachable) is /readiness's job,
not this one. An orchestrator should restart the process on liveness
failure, but must not do that just because Postgres/Redis is briefly
unreachable — that's a readiness problem, not a process-health one.

Whether this instance can actually serve traffic right now — real
checks against PostgreSQL and Redis, never a hardcoded 200. Returns
HTTP 503 (not 200) when a critical dependency is unavailable, so a
load balancer/orchestrator actually stops routing traffic here rather
than being told everything is fine.

Real, in-process request metrics (see app/metrics.py) plus real queue
depth/worker status (see app/queue.py) — admin-only since request
volume/route breakdown is operationally sensitive. No Prometheus/
OpenTelemetry exporter is configured in this environment; that
limitation is stated explicitly in the response rather than silently
omitted.

Real gateway status: which providers exist (Groq/OpenAI/Azure/Anthropic/
Vertex/Bedrock), which one is currently active, and the last genuinely
successful call this process has logged — never simulated.

Real backend search across repositories, scans, findings, controls,
dependencies, AI providers, users, and audit events — every result
comes from a live PostgreSQL query (see app/services/search.py), never
from data already sitting in the browser. Results are capped per
category so the response stays small regardless of database size, and
every category is filtered to the caller's own tenant — search must
never surface another tenant's data, even as a search "hit".

post.description:
Creates the scan record + all stage rows as 'queued', enqueues the real
pipeline job on the Redis queue, and returns immediately. The actual
work happens in a separate worker process — nothing here blocks on the
scan finishing. The scan is owned by the caller's own tenant
(principal.tenant_id), never a tenant id supplied in the request body.

delete.description:
Clears only the caller's own tenant's scans — this must never be
able to wipe another tenant's data, even for an admin account.

post.description:
Scan an uploaded ZIP archive of a repository (the blueprint's second intake path). The archive is untrusted: it is
validated here (real ZIP, no path traversal / encryption / bomb-sized members) before anything is queued, stored in the
database so the separate worker can read it, extracted by the worker under the same size/count limits as a clone, and
deleted again when the scan finishes. Nothing in it is ever executed.

Admin-only. Registers a webhook endpoint for this tenant and returns its signing secret EXACTLY ONCE (it is derived,
not stored — delete and recreate the integration to rotate it).
Public endpoint called by GitHub/GitLab — authenticated ONLY by the delivery's signature, never by a user session.

get.description:
Server-Sent Events stream of real stage transitions. Replays current
DB state first (so a client that connects after the job already made
progress isn't stuck showing nothing), then relays live Redis pub/sub
messages published by the worker as it runs. Closes once the scan
reaches a terminal state.

Real, tenant-scoped Server-Sent Events stream of finding-related
activity (review actions, reclassification, new findings from a
completed scan) — the SAME Redis pub/sub mechanism as
/scans/{scan_id}/events, just subscribed to a tenant-wide channel
(see app.events.subscribe_findings) instead of one scan's channel,
since the Findings list spans every scan in the tenant.

The channel is derived from `principal.tenant_id` (resolved
server-side from the verified JWT) — never from a client-supplied
parameter — so this endpoint cannot be made to stream another
tenant's events no matter what a caller passes.

Long-lived by design (the Findings list may be open indefinitely);
the idle-heartbeat/give-up behavior mirrors the scan-events endpoint
so the frontend's reconnect logic only has to handle one shape of
"the stream ended, reconnect."

Real, tenant-scoped Server-Sent Events stream of AI Activity (POST
/runtime/events ingestion) — the SAME Redis pub/sub + StreamingResponse
mechanism as /findings/events (see app.events.subscribe_runtime_activity),
on its own tenant-wide channel so a raw activity event and a governance
finding are never conflated on the wire. This is what makes the AI
Activity page genuinely real-time instead of relying on its 15s poll
for new rows; the poll remains only as a fallback for when this
connection is down.

Payload is bounded, safe metadata only (event_id/event_type/
application_id/provider/model/trace_id/span_id/latency_ms/
input_tokens/output_tokens/policy_result) — never a raw prompt,
response, or content_preview value (see app.main.ingest_runtime_event).

The channel is derived from `principal.tenant_id` (resolved
server-side from the verified JWT/runtime credential) — never from a
client-supplied parameter — so this endpoint cannot be made to stream
another tenant's events no matter what a caller passes.

Real scan-to-scan diff (see app/services/scan_compare.py) — findings,
dependencies, AI components, controls, and (when both scans have a
persisted evidence graph) graph nodes/edges. `scan_id` is treated as
the baseline ("A") and `other_scan_id` as the comparison ("B"), so
"added" means present in B but not A. Both scans must belong to the
caller's own tenant — _load_scan_bundle enforces this for each one
independently, so comparing across tenants is impossible even if the
caller somehow knows another tenant's scan id.

delete.description:
Clears only the caller's own tenant's runtime telemetry (events + the findings derived from them) — never
another tenant's data. Registered applications (RuntimeApplication) and credentials are configuration, not
telemetry, and are deliberately left alone: clearing usage history should not silently revoke a real
integration's ability to keep sending events.

post.description:
Real runtime/AI-activity telemetry ingestion. Idempotent on
(tenant_id, event_id) — re-posting the same event_id returns the
already-persisted result rather than re-running detection or creating
a duplicate row. Synchronous: detection is deterministic pattern/
allowlist matching (see app.services.runtime_detection), not an LLM
call, so there is no latency reason to queue it — keeping this path
minimal rather than adding infrastructure that would just add hops.

Accepts EITHER a real human JWT session OR a real runtime service
credential (`Authorization: Bearer rsc_<id>.<secret>` — see
app.services.runtime_auth and POST /runtime/credentials), the
production-appropriate identity for an AI gateway/application with
no human session. `caller.tenant_id` is resolved from whichever real
credential was presented — never from anything in the request body,
so cross-tenant event injection is impossible by construction. A
credential bound to one application_id may only ingest events for
that exact application.

get.description:
Real, tenant-scoped, paginated raw runtime event stream — for the AI
Activity view (deliberately separate from Findings: most of these
rows are normal telemetry, not governance violations). Never returns
content_preview (a caller-supplied bounded PII-risk excerpt) — only
the structural/routing fields already needed to explain each real
event. `real_findings_count` for a row is the actual number of
RuntimeFinding rows that event produced (usually 0).

Tenant-scoped: an admin only sees their own tenant's audit events.
Platform-level events (e.g. tenant_created) have tenant_id=NULL and are
intentionally excluded here — they are not any single tenant's data.
The repository directory behind the Overview filter — derived from this tenant's real scans (see app.services.repositories).

Real, server-side, cross-scan findings list — see
app/services/findings_query.py. Bounded by page_size (never the whole
result set), tenant-scoped, filtered and searched entirely in SQL.
Comma-separated values are accepted for severity/classification/
status/source (e.g. `severity=CRITICAL,ERROR`) so the frontend can
select multiple values per filter, matching the Architecture command
center's existing multi-select filter pattern. `sort=priority`
(default) surfaces attention-worthy findings first using real
severity/classification/status fields; `sort=recent` sorts by scan
recency only. `governance_relevant=true` excludes raw detection
signals that aren't themselves a real governance conclusion — see
findings_query.list_findings's docstring.

Real aggregate counts (total/open/critical/high/confirmed-sensitive/
needs-review) for this tenant's findings — the single source of truth
the Overview page's finding counters should read from, computed with
the exact same severity/classification derivation as the findings
list itself (previously the Overview page recomputed its own,
Semgrep-only severity count, disagreeing with what the Findings page
showed for the same data).

Real distinct filter option values currently present in this
tenant's findings — populated from the database, never a hardcoded
list that could drift from what values the classification pipeline
actually produces.

Full evidence chain for a triaged (URL) finding: classification, the
deterministic facts and rules that produced it, AI reasoning + the
guardrails applied to it, evidence items, policy/control references,
runtime evidence, review dispositions and the complete classification
history. 404 for findings that are not triaged.

post.description:
Human override of a triaged finding's classification/status. Requires a
reason, keeps the previous values in the append-only history, is written
to the audit log, and is never silently replaced by a later automatic
re-analysis.

(Re)analyse one scan's raw URL signals with the current rules. Purely
additive — raw evidence is untouched; changes append classification
history. Without `run_ai` the run is synchronous and returns the summary;
with `run_ai` it continues in the background (rows show ai_status
pending -> analyzing -> analyzed and update live over SSE).

Safe migration/reclassification of EXISTING findings: analyses the raw
URL signals of every completed scan of this tenant. Original detections,
review history and audit history are read, never modified.

Reprocesses this scan's already-persisted raw Presidio detections
through the CURRENT context-aware classification pipeline (see
app/services/finding_classification.py) — without re-cloning or
re-scanning the repository. Every field the classifier needs
(entity_type, path, redacted_snippet, confidence) was already captured
and persisted at scan time.

Never fabricates a replacement finding: only the classification/
severity/context fields on each EXISTING raw detection are recomputed.
Writes NEW Evidence rows (the same append-only pattern every other
pipeline stage uses — see pipeline._persist_evidence) rather than
mutating the originals, so the original raw detections stay traceable.
Also recomputes the sensitive_data governance control, since a
corrected pii_count can change its pass/review/fail outcome.

get.description:
Real runtime-telemetry connection state — never a hardcoded
"connected". `connected` is only true when a real event arrived
within RUNTIME_CONNECTED_WINDOW_MINUTES; an event from days ago
reports connected=false with a real last_event_at timestamp, not a
stale "still live" claim.

Real AI usage/consumption rollup for the AI Usage analytics page —
see app.services.governance.get_runtime_usage_summary. Aggregates
the SAME real RuntimeEvent telemetry as /governance/applications and
/governance/models, bucketed by real time (hour or day, chosen from
the actual requested span) and grouped by application/model/
provider, instead of the raw per-event rows /runtime/events
returns — this platform had no time-series/dashboard-scale
aggregation endpoint before this one, and charting usage over time
by downloading every event into the browser doesn't scale.
`pricing_configured` is always false today — no pricing/cost
infrastructure exists anywhere in this backend; the frontend must
gate every dollar figure on that flag and never compute one itself.

post.description:
Admin-only, explicit registration of a real AI application identity
(see app.models.RuntimeApplication). Upsert semantics — registering
an already-known application_id again just updates its display_name,
matching the same idempotent-PUT pattern PUT /runtime/policy already
uses. Ingesting a runtime event NEVER calls this — an unregistered
application_id is shown as "UNKNOWN APPLICATION", never silently
turned into a registry row.

put.description:
Admin-only, explicit, audited statement that an AI application is built from a repository. Runtime telemetry carries
no repository key, so this owner-confirmed link is the ONLY thing that ties an application (and its models, runtime
controls and runtime findings) to a repository in the Overview's repository filter. The repository id is validated
against this tenant's scans. Linking an application that is only observed in telemetry registers it.

get.description:
ONE consistent, repository-scoped snapshot for the four Overview KPI cards — every number comes from the same
scoped queries the detail sections use (findings_query / governance), so a card and its detail can never disagree,
and a repository switch changes all four together. Nothing here is hardcoded or estimated.

The complete platform architecture (zones, components, relationships) discovered from the running code and joined with live runtime state —
see app.services.architecture_platform. Nothing is stored or mocked; secrets are never included.

The Architecture module's entity graph — a projection of the canonical Evidence Graph data plus scans, branches, runtime metrics and
derived-but-provable relationships (see app.services.architecture_graph). `repository_id` / `scan_id` are validated against THIS tenant
(404 otherwise; 400 for a scan that is not completed). Every node and edge carries the views (system / ai / repository / governance /
dataflow / dependency / evidence) it belongs to, so switching view needs no other data. Nothing is stored or mocked.

One unified graph of every scanned repository's discovered structure: repositories, applications, technologies
(databases, caches, queues, cloud SDKs, AI providers), infrastructure. Every edge carries its real evidence and a
confidence. See app.services.discovery_graph.

The architecture agent: a plain-English explanation of the same discovery graph, built only from its facts
(app.services.architecture_agent). Runs on demand, never on page load.

post.description:
The architecture narrator: one spoken sentence per diagram step (a component or a connection), written from the
steps' own facts. The client sends the platform diagram's steps; the model may only speak about the ids it was given
(app.services.architecture_agent.narrate). Runs on demand, when a user presses Explain.

get.description:
One repository's own real architecture — languages, frameworks, databases, external services, and (only when actually
detected) AI providers/models/frameworks/vector stores, classified into a small set of real components (never a fixed
template forced onto every repository — see app.services.repo_architecture). Reuses the same evidence
architecture_platform._repo_structure already computes; nothing here is a second detection pipeline. 404 if
`repository_id` does not belong to this tenant.

A REAL import-dependency graph for one folder of one repository — which of that folder's files import which
other real files, and which real files elsewhere import FROM it, resolved purely from the literal import
statements discovery already parsed for this repository's latest completed scan (see
app.services.repo_architecture.build_folder_dependency_graph). `path=""` means the repository root.

The real per-file discovery evidence behind the Overview "Files Scanned" KPI — the exact same file list
app.services.discovery already persisted (Evidence.kind='discovery') for each repository's LATEST COMPLETED
scan, the same scan _overview_files_scanned sums file_count from. Nothing here is a second discovery pass.

Real AI application inventory — see app.services.governance's module
docstring. Every field is either a real aggregate over real
RuntimeEvent/RuntimeFinding rows for this tenant, or explicitly
UNKNOWN/null when no real evidence establishes it (never inferred).
Real (provider, model) inventory — see app.services.governance.
Per-model governance posture (controls summary, risk dimensions, change count) — see app.services.model_governance.
Full governance detail for one observed (provider, model). Query params because model ids contain '/'.
Per-application governance status: worst of the application's runtime control results.

Frameworks a control mapping can be labelled with, and the platform controls they can map to.
Mapping is a labelling aid: the platform makes NO certification or compliance claim.

post.description:
Upload a governance PDF. Text-based PDFs only (no OCR). Not authoritative for evidence evaluation
unless `authoritative` is set here or later by someone with manage_governance.

delete.description:
Archive by default (kept, hidden, excluded from evidence evaluation). `hard=true` permanently deletes an
ALREADY ARCHIVED document with its extracted sections and controls.

patch.description: Confirm / edit the mapping of an extracted requirement to platform controls and framework references.

get.description:
Framework reference -> policy requirement -> platform control -> evidence status, from CONFIRMED mappings only.
Status comes from the latest completed scan's real control evaluation (NOT_EVALUATED when there is none).

Named, external AI-governance frameworks (OWASP LLM Top 10, NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act,
ISO/IEC 42001, SOC 2, GDPR, HIPAA) pre-mapped to this platform's own real controls —
see app.services.framework_catalog. Distinct from /governance/framework-map, which
links a tenant's OWN uploaded policy documents to controls one confirmed mapping at a
time; this is a fixed public reference catalog, evaluated live against this tenant's
real control statuses. A category with no mapped control reads "Not covered" — never
guessed, never silently hidden.

Per-repository evidence coverage from the latest completed scan's persisted evidence — definition,
thresholds and per-detector status are in app/services/repo_coverage.py. Unknown when not measurable.

Deterministic Evidence Graph / ER diagram metadata — see
app.services.diagram. Built only from this tenant's stored data (scans,
evidence, persisted scan graph, findings, reviews, runtime telemetry);
no LLM decides what is related. `entity_type` is a comma-separated
filter; `depth` limits hops from repository nodes.

Read-only drill-down behind a control card — the real rows its status rests on
(see governance.get_control_evidence). Never changes a control's status.

Real, deterministic governance controls — the existing static
per-scan OPA rollup (rules/policies.rego) plus a real runtime
control catalog mapped to already-real runtime_detection rule_ids
(see app.services.governance). UNKNOWN/NOT_EVALUATED whenever this
tenant has no real evidence relevant to a control — never silently
PASS.

The AI inventory registry: one row per repository of the caller's tenant (AI yes/no, providers, models, review level, live traffic)
plus the header counts — each row summarises that repository's model card (app.services.model_cards).

Model & system card of ONE repository, built only from its latest completed scan's evidence (app.services.model_cards): detected
languages, AI providers, literal model names, call patterns, data detections, the repository's AI-behaviour controls, and the
facts only an owner can confirm (marked OWNER_ANSWER_NEEDED). `status: no_completed_scan` when there is nothing to base it on.

The blueprint's 30 first governance checks, evaluated from the evidence of each repository's latest completed scan
(see app.services.check_coverage). A check with no detector says NO_DETECTOR; a check whose scanner did not run says
UNKNOWN; nothing is ever defaulted to a pass. Scoped to one repository, or every repository of the caller's tenant.

post.description:
Admin-only. Creates a real service-to-service ingestion credential
(see app.services.runtime_auth) and returns the RAW secret exactly
once, in this response — it is never retrievable again, and only its
hash is stored. `application_id`, if given, must already be a
registered application (see POST /runtime/applications) — a
credential is never bound to an unregistered/arbitrary app name.

get.description:
Never returns secret_hash or the raw secret — only
secret_prefix (safe partial identification) and real usage/lifecycle
metadata.

put.description:
Admin-only, real, tenant-configurable runtime governance policy —
never hardcoded into the frontend (see app.models.RuntimePolicy).

post.description:
A concrete, evidence-grounded fix suggestion for ONE real finding — text only, never writes anything. The
finding is always re-derived from the scan's real evidence here, exactly like explain_finding above.

Writes a REAL fix for ONE finding — reads the repository's real current content, asks the LLM for an exact
patch, applies it, commits and pushes. Hard-gated to repositories hosted on this project's own local dev git
server (see app/services/finding_fix.py's module docstring) — a real external repository (GitHub, ...) always
gets a clean "unsupported" response here, never a write attempt, regardless of what a caller asks for.

A concrete fix suggestion for ONE real AI-governance issue (see app.services.ai_governance_findings). The
issue is always re-derived from the scan's real evidence here — never trusted from the client — so a caller
cannot ask the model to "explain" a fabricated issue that doesn't actually exist in this scan's evidence.

A real, on-demand AI insight for ONE component of the per-repository architecture diagram — the component is
always re-derived here from the repository's own current evidence (never trusted from the client), same
discipline as suggest_ai_governance_fix, so a caller can never ask the model to "explain" a component that
doesn't actually exist in this repository's real evidence. Never pre-generated for every component on page
load — only called when a reviewer actually clicks one, same cost/latency discipline as every other
on-demand explain action on the platform.

get.description:
Bounded 'expand this node' data — real BFS over persisted edges,
capped by `depth` so a dense graph never sends the whole graph to the
browser just to explore one node's surroundings.

Real review status per finding graph node — a single bulk query over
review_dispositions (see graph_query.get_finding_review_status), never
one request per finding. `possible_values` is derived from the actual
ReviewDisposition.action values this platform records, not invented
status names, so the frontend filter can populate itself dynamically.

Real directional impact analysis (see app/services/graph_query.py
compute_impact) — upstream/downstream reachability over persisted
edges, never an inferred or estimated blast radius.

Looks an edge up by its natural key — what the frontend's graph view
actually has on hand (it still renders from the per-scan JSONB evidence
blob for backward compatibility with scans predating persistent
graph_nodes/graph_edges, so it never carries a numeric edge row id).

action.title: Action
action.description: One of: accept, assign_owner, comment, create_ticket, dispute, mark_reviewed, request_evidence

git_url.title: Git Url
git_url.description: HTTPS Git URL to clone, e.g. https://github.com/org/repo.git

admin_username.title: Admin Username
admin_username.description: If set (with admin_password), provisions this tenant's first admin user atomically.

RuntimeCredentialCreateRequest.title: RuntimeCredentialCreateRequest
RuntimeCredentialCreateRequest.description:
Admin-only — see POST /runtime/credentials. `expires_in_days=None`
means no expiration; a production integration should still set a
real value and rotate, but this is not forced so a short-lived local
test harness credential doesn't need one.

RuntimeEventRequest.title: RuntimeEventRequest
RuntimeEventRequest.description:
One real runtime/AI-activity event — see app.models.RuntimeEvent and
app.services.runtime_detection. `event_id` is the caller's own
idempotency key (their tracing system's real id); re-posting the same
one is a no-op, never a duplicate. `content_preview`, if supplied, is
a short, ALREADY-bounded excerpt the caller chose to share — never
the full prompt/response — used only to run real detectors against.

There is deliberately no client-supplied timestamp field — `received_at`
is always set server-side (see the route below), so a malformed or
spoofed client clock can never enter the system as though it were
authoritative.
